proximal_policy_optimization.summary: A policy learns when to be short, flat or long by trading the training span, improving in small clipped steps so one rollout cannot pull it too far.
proximal_policy_optimization.implementationNote: Bridge: PPO (Stable-Baselines3) with a clipped surrogate and generalised advantages. P(up) = pi(long)/(pi(long)+pi(short)), not a fitted probability. Differs from the spec: the market ignores the agent, whose position is not in its state: cost-aware reward maximisation on the train span's price tape (next-open fills); each decision's reward is its whole h-bar trade. Expect: an edge only where the features predict the h-bar move.

native.produces: Proximal policy optimisation outputs an actor network that gives a probability to each of hold, long and short in the current state, and a separate critic network that estimates the return expected from that state.
native.targetVariable: the discounted sum of future rewards the agent collects by following its own stochastic policy from each state of the trading environment
native.objectiveNote: This member maximises a clipped surrogate: the ratio of the new to the old probability of each taken action is cut off at the clip range before it multiplies the generalised advantage estimate, which lets one rollout be reused for several passes, and a value regression term and an entropy bonus are summed into the same loss.

metrics.why: The actor is trained only to earn reward, so what its own most probable action of hold, long or short earns per decision on bars that no rollout ever visited is the direct test of the clipped updates.
metrics.baseline: staying flat on every bar, and the same policy's reward on its training span

metrics.why: Rollouts are sampled actions and minibatches are shuffled, so two runs that differ only in seed follow different paths through the clipped updates, and the spread of their test reward tells a real edge from one fortunate run.
metrics.baseline: the same agent on the same series with only the seed changed

metrics.why: The generalised advantage estimate is the rollout's reward measured against the critic's guess, so a critic that explains none of the variance of the returns hands the clipped surrogate advantages that are mostly noise.
metrics.baseline: a critic that predicts the mean return of the rollout for every state

metrics.why: The entropy bonus in the combined loss exists to keep the actor from putting all its probability on one action too soon, and the mean entropy of its three action probabilities shows whether that happened.
metrics.baseline: the natural logarithm of three, the entropy of choosing among three actions evenly

metrics.why: If the kept actor is chosen by its reward on held-back bars across rollouts, that reward is a maximum over rollouts and flatters by construction, so it is read beside the test reward for that reason and never in place of it.

The specification names the clip fraction, the share of sampled actions whose probability ratio left the clip band during an update, as the method's own built-in diagnostic: a share near zero says the clip range could widen, and a persistently high share says the clip is containing an instability only partly.
When the reward after costs is small the clipped updates can settle on holding nearly always, and the share of bars on which the actor prefers long, short and hold shows whether it trades at all.

The reward collected per rollout, traced over rollouts, shows whether the repeated passes under the clip kept improving the policy or whether it stopped moving, which is a statement about convergence and not about skill.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: The clipped surrogate maximises expected discounted reward and contains no spread of returns, so the ratio grades the trading rule and costs of the backtester and is an as-run number.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: Nothing in the actor's loss separates losing bars from winning ones, so a downside-only ratio describes the traded path and not what the agent optimised.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: The advantage estimate sums discounted rewards and is blind to the depth of a losing run, so drawdown is measured only on the as-run equity path.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: It needs closed trades, and when a trade opens and closes is decided by the engine that runs the policy and not by the actor's action probabilities.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: It is a sizing recipe and not a measurement, and the actor chooses among hold, long and short with no size.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The actor's probability of long says how much it prefers that action for reward, shaped by costs and the entropy bonus, and it was never fitted to how often price rises.

notApplicable.name: Price forecast error
notApplicable.why: Neither the actor nor the critic forecasts a price move, since the critic estimates reward and not points.

notApplicable.name: Predicted action value minus realised return
notApplicable.why: The critic estimates the value of a state under the current policy and never the value of each action, so there is no maximum over learned action values to be optimistic about.

asRun.standInNote: The optimiser is the specification's own, the Stable-Baselines3 implementation with a clipped surrogate, generalised advantage estimates, several optimisation passes over shuffled minibatches of each rollout, separate actor and critic networks and an entropy bonus. The environment is not the specification's: it is a fixed reward tape on which the observation is the bar's own feature row, the market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state, and each decision is paid at once as one whole trade over the label horizon net of a round trip. The as-run numbers therefore measure cost-aware reward-weighted direction calls and not sequential position management.
asRun.probabilityNote: The actor network gives softmax shares for short, flat and long from the bar's feature row, and the probability of up is the long share divided by the sum of the long and short shares, with the flat share discarded and nothing fitted to outcomes.

stepQuantity.unit: on training rows minus the mean net reward per decision of the actions sampled during the rollout, in move-scale units, which is the reward collected and not the clipped surrogate itself; on validation rows nats of the long share

meaningful.why: The clipped updates were driven by the net reward of whole trades, so the money made by trading the side the actor prefers between long and short is the as-run number closest to what the agent was trained for, read against buy and hold on the same folds.

It measures how steadily the actor's preferred side earned per bar after costs, which tests whether the repeated passes over each rollout learned something that repeats or fitted a few rewarding stretches of the tape.
An actor trained through a rising span can learn to prefer long everywhere, and subtracting buy and hold on the same folds shows what its reading of the feature row added beyond that lean.

The advantage estimates pay each decision as a separate trade and never show the actor a run of losses on an open position, so the deepest hole on the marked-to-market path is a risk it was never trained to see.

It compares what the winning trades opened by the actor's preferred side made with what the losing ones gave back after costs, read with the trade count because an actor that rarely changes side produces few trades.
It counts how many trades opened when the actor changed side ended in profit, which describes the shape of the result while the engine's holding rule and not the agent decides when each trade ends.
When the actor's long and short shares sit close together the call flips on small changes in the feature row, and this turnover shows how much of the result that churn handed to costs.
It counts how often the actor's long share crossed its short share, and every trading number of this agent is read with it beside the predicted up share.
It shows how often the actor preferred long to short, which exposes a policy that settled on one side for the whole test span instead of reading the features.

The hard call is up whenever the actor's long share is at least its short share, so the hit rate tests whether the side reward taught it to prefer is also the side price went, against calling the fold's training majority direction.

Clipped updates on a trending tape can leave the actor preferring one side on every bar, and averaging the hit rate on up bars and on down bars shows whether its preference changes with the feature row.
It sums up in one symmetric number whether the actor's preferred side moves with the actual direction, with zero meaning the preference carries nothing beyond a fixed lean.

The long share over long plus short is a continuous number, so this shows whether bars where the actor prefers long more strongly are more often up bars, using the ordering alone and not treating the share as stated odds.

The outer search over network size, learning rate, discount factor, entropy coefficient and clip range is scored on blocks of the training span with the real simulator, so its best value is a flattering selection score shown beside the test result.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The long share is a preference shaped by reward after costs and by the entropy bonus and was never fitted to how often price rises, so scoring it as odds measures how sharp the actor is and not how honest.
It grades the actor's long share as if it were a probability of an up bar, and the actor was trained to earn reward, so a good or bad value says nothing about its decisions.
Calibration compares stated odds with observed frequencies, and the actor's long share was never meant to equal the frequency of up bars.
The slope of outcomes on the log-odds of the long share reads the strength of the entropy coefficient and the scale of the reward, not an over-confident or timid forecaster.
It is built on the Brier score of a preference share and on a hindsight up share of the test bars, so neither half refers to anything the agent stated.
Not computed because there is no price model: the actor outputs action shares and the critic estimates reward, never a size of move.
Not computed because there is no price model, so no forecast in points exists to measure a miss on.
Not computed because there is no price model, so there is no forecast whose sign could be compared with the actual move.
The training curve holds minus the reward collected during the rollout while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the long share, so their difference compares two different quantities.

With the long-only setting off and no stop or target the engine is always long or short once the first trade opens, so the share describes the engine's rule and hides every bar on which the actor preferred flat.

caveats: The market does not react to the agent and the agent's position is not in the state, so each decision is rewarded as one fixed trade over the label horizon and nothing in training resembles managing an open position.

The engine overrides the agent's flat action, its sizing and its holding period: the traded side is whichever of long and short has the larger share even on bars where flat was the actor's first choice, and training charged a round trip on every non-flat decision while the engine keeps a position in the same direction without paying again.

The discount factor and the generalised advantage estimate add the rewards of the following bars of the episode to each decision, although on this tape an action changes nothing about what the later bars pay, so that part of the advantage is noise the critic has to absorb.

The kept policy is the one whose most probable action, flat included, earned the highest mean net reward on the validation tape across rollouts, which is an optimistic maximum and is scored on a different action rule from the long or short call the engine trades.
A bar with a missing feature value gets no prediction and the engine holds the existing position through it.
Consecutive decisions share future bars because each reward spans the label horizon, so intervals around these numbers need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.

The trading numbers follow the run's own long-only, holding bars, stop loss ticks, take profit ticks and contracts settings, the last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open, and for roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's figure applied as a stated assumption.

It counts how many trades created by the policy's call flips ended positive, a companion to the profit factor since the advantage weights actions by payoff size and not by frequency.

It tells how many closed trades stand behind the trading numbers, which for a policy with few call flips can be a small sample.
It shows whether the batched update drove the policy to prefer long over short on nearly every bar, the collapse the entropy coefficient is there to prevent.

It condenses the policy's long and short calls against the realised direction into one number that falls to zero when the policy has collapsed onto a single side.
It asks whether bars where the policy leans harder toward long over short went up more often, testing the ordering of its preference without reading its size as a probability.
The search over network size, learning rate, discount factor and entropy coefficient is scored on training-span blocks only, so its best value is optimistic and is read beside the test result.

batch_size.label: Batch size
batch_size.description: How many transitions one gradient step averages over.

gradient_clipping_norm.label: Gradient clipping norm
gradient_clipping_norm.description: The largest gradient norm one update may take (0 = no clipping).

training_sweeps.label: Training sweeps
training_sweeps.description: How many times the agent walks the training span's bars (environment steps = sweeps x bars).

native.produces: A policy over trading actions, read from a state built by encoding each kind of input separately, fusing the encodings with cross-modal attention and carrying the result through time with a recurrent or transformer module.
native.targetVariable: The discounted sum of future trading reward collected by the actions the policy chooses from the fused multi-modal state.
native.objectiveNote: The specification's reinforcement-learning variant maximises discounted reward with a policy-gradient or actor-critic update and adds weighted helper losses that pretrain each modality encoder, and it also allows a supervised or symbolic reasoning head in place of the policy.

metrics.why: The reasoning head is trained to earn reward from the fused state, so the direct test is the mean reward of the action it prefers, flat included, on bars where the encoders, the attention and the policy were neither trained nor selected.
metrics.baseline: Zero reward per decision, which is what staying flat on every bar of the same tape pays.

metrics.why: The policy samples its actions during training and learns through several encoders and an attention layer at once, so two runs with different seeds can settle on different habits, and one run alone is weak evidence.
metrics.baseline: The spread of the same agent's test reward across reruns that differ only in seed.

metrics.why: In the actor-critic variant the value head sets the advantage that scales every policy step, so a value head that explains none of the realised reward means the modality encoders are being trained on noise.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value for a critic that predicts the mean reward on every bar.

metrics.why: It shows whether the action shares coming out of the fused state still vary with the inputs or have frozen onto one action early, which would make the encoders and the attention irrelevant to the decision.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of the number of actions, which is the entropy of a policy with no preference.

metrics.why: The kept weights are the ones that earned the most on a validation stretch, so that validation reward is flattered by the choosing and is shown only to be compared with the reward on the untouched test bars.
metrics.baseline: The same agent's mean reward on the test tape of the same fold.

metrics.why: The cross-modal attention is meant to weigh price, text and graph inputs differently as conditions change, and this shows whether it does so or pours nearly all weight onto one input, leaving the agent multi-modal in name only.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of the number of modalities, which is the entropy of equal attention.

notApplicable.name: Directional Edge
notApplicable.why: The reasoning head chooses actions to earn reward and may stay flat, so a hit rate on the sign of the forward return is not what the specification trains or judges.

notApplicable.name: Confidence Edge
notApplicable.why: The policy's action shares are reward-shaped preferences rather than conviction about direction, so ranking bars by them is not this agent's own measure.

notApplicable.name: Gaussian NLL Loss
notApplicable.why: The specification's objective is discounted reward plus helper losses for the encoders, and its policy outputs no mean and variance of the return for a Gaussian likelihood to score.

notApplicable.name: Volatility-Adjusted RMSE
notApplicable.why: Price prediction appears in the specification only as a pretraining helper for the time-series encoder, while the agent's product is an action with no forecast error of its own.

notApplicable.name: Top-Decile Directional Edge
notApplicable.why: There is no stated confidence about direction to take a top tenth of, because the reasoning head outputs action shares shaped by reward.

notApplicable.name: Brier Score
notApplicable.why: A Brier score grades a probability that price rises, and the policy states a preference among actions that was never fitted to that frequency.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The share of long among the policy's actions is a preference shaped by reward and by the entropy bonus, not an estimate of how often price rises, so a forecast-odds score grades something the agent never claimed.

notApplicable.name: Expected calibration error
notApplicable.why: Calibration asks whether stated odds match observed frequencies, and the policy's action shares were never fitted to frequencies of up and down bars.

notApplicable.name: Gain over the flat agent of the same learner
notApplicable.why: This agent has a single policy head and no subgoals or options, so there is no hierarchy to switch off and compare against.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable agent keeps the specification's shape, with one encoder per input group, cross-modal attention at every bar, a gated recurrent unit over the window and an actor-critic head, but its modalities are groups of this instrument's feature columns plus calendar channels rather than raw text, images or graphs, news sentiment is present on only a small share of bars, and the environment is a fixed reward tape: the market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state, so every decision is paid as one whole trade over the label horizon and the as-run numbers measure cost-aware reward-weighted direction calls.
asRun.probabilityNote: The policy head gives softmax shares for short, flat and long from the recurrent state of the last bar of the window, and the probability of up is the long share divided by the sum of the long and short shares, with the flat share discarded and nothing fitted to outcomes.

stepQuantity.unit: on training rows a mixed loss in move-scale reward units (the advantage-weighted actor term, half the squared advantage of the critic, minus the entropy bonus, plus the weighted Huber term of the price head); on validation rows nats of the long share

meaningful.why: The actor-critic head is trained on the net reward of whole trades, so the money made by trading the side the policy prefers between long and short is the as-run number closest to what the agent was trained for, read against buy and hold on the same folds and with the agent's own flat choice overridden.

It measures how steadily the policy's preferred side earned money per bar after costs, which tests whether the fused encoders found something repeatable or the reward came from a few lucky stretches of the tape.

The reward the agent learned from pays each decision as a separate trade and never shows it a run of losses in a row, so the deepest hole on the marked-to-market path is a risk the policy was never trained to see.

It compares what the winning trades opened by the policy's preferred side made with what the losing ones gave back after costs, read with the trade count because a policy that rarely changes side produces few trades.

It counts how many trades opened when the policy changed side ended in profit, which describes the shape of the trading result, while the engine's holding rule and not the agent decides when each trade ends.
A sampled policy whose long and short shares hover close together flips side on small changes in the window, and this turnover shows how much of the result that churn handed to costs.
It counts how often the long share crossed the short share, and every trading number of this agent is read with it beside the predicted up share.
It shows how often the policy preferred long to short, which exposes an agent that learned to sit on one side through the whole test span instead of reading its modalities.

The hard call is up whenever the long share is at least the short share, so the hit rate tests whether the side the reward taught the policy to prefer is also the side price went, against calling the fold's training majority direction.

A policy trained on reward through a trending stretch can learn to prefer one side on every bar, and averaging the hit rate on up bars and on down bars shows whether its preference changes with what the encoders read.
It sums up in one symmetric number whether the policy's preferred side moves with the actual direction, with zero meaning the preference carries nothing beyond a fixed lean.

The long share over long plus short is a continuous number, so this shows whether bars where the policy prefers long more strongly are more often up bars, a use of the ordering alone that does not treat the share as stated odds.

The price line comes from a second training pass of the same network design whose auxiliary price head is selected on validation Huber loss, so this tests that second pass's size forecast against forecasting no move and says nothing about the weights that make the traded call.

It gives in points the typical miss of the forecast from the second training pass of the network, whose auxiliary price head is selected on validation Huber loss, read beside the no-change forecast's miss on the same bars.
It checks the sign of the auxiliary head's forecast, which is trained on the move itself with no costs, so it can disagree with the policy's preferred side that was trained on reward after costs.
It is the selection score that chose the learning rate, discount factor, entropy coefficient and modality dropout on training blocks, flattered by that choosing and shown only beside the test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The long share is a preference shaped by reward, by costs and by the entropy bonus and was never fitted to how often price rises, so scoring it as forecast odds measures how sharp the policy is and not how honest.
It grades the long share as if it were a probability of an up bar, and the policy head was trained to earn reward, so a good or bad value says nothing about the agent's decisions.
Calibration compares stated odds with observed frequencies, and the policy's action shares were never meant to equal the frequency of up bars.
The slope of outcomes on the log-odds of the long share reads the strength of the entropy bonus and of the reward scale, not an over-confident or timid forecaster.
It is built on the Brier score of a preference share and on a hindsight up share of the test bars, so neither half refers to anything the agent stated.

The training curve holds the mixed actor, critic, entropy and Huber loss while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the long share, so their difference compares two different quantities.

With the long-only setting off the engine never goes flat once in a trade, so this share reflects the engine overriding the agent's flat action and not how often the policy wanted to be in the market.

caveats: The market does not react to the agent and the agent's position is not in the state, so each decision is rewarded as one fixed trade over the label horizon and nothing in training resembles managing an open position.

The engine overrides the agent's own flat action, its sizing and its holding period: the traded side is long whenever the long share is at least the short share, even on bars where flat was the policy's most preferred action.

The kept epoch of the direction model is the one whose most preferred action, flat included, earned the highest mean net reward on the validation tape, which is not the long-versus-short rule the engine then trades.

The price forecast comes from a second training pass of the same network whose kept epoch is chosen on the validation Huber loss of the auxiliary head, so the forecast line and the traded call do not come from the same weights.

The modalities are groups of this instrument's feature columns plus calendar channels, and the news sentiment group is empty on most bars, so the cross-modal attention mostly weighs price, volume and volatility groups against each other.
Bars without a complete window of past bars get no prediction and the engine holds the existing position through them.
Consecutive decisions share future bars because each reward spans the label horizon, so intervals around these numbers need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.

The trading numbers follow the run's own long-only, holding bars, stop loss ticks, take profit ticks and contracts settings, the last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open, and for roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's figure applied as a stated assumption.
